Seminar Title:

Stability Assessment of Underground Structures under Overlying Goaf and Barrier Pillars during Mechanised Depillaring: A Field and Numerical Modelling Studies

Seminar Type:

Departmental Seminar

Department:

Mining Engineering

Speaker Name:

Tamilprasanth M (525mn6002)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

Mining Department Seminar Hall

Date and Time:

09 Oct 2026 04.15 PM

Contact:

Dr. Mahesh Kumar Shriwas

Abstract:

Underground mining of multiple coal seam encounters severe ground control challenges during ex-traction of lower seam with caving under weak/laminated interburden parting and staggered layout of panels. Previous studies have shown that interaction of multiple seams can lead to geotechnical hazards, including roof and rib failure, pillar instability, floor heave and coal bump. In this study, a detailed case analysis of undermining in an Indian coal mine is presented, where severe instability of pillar, fender and immediate roof observed near the line of extraction during continuous miner-based mechanised depillaring. The No. 5 Seam (working seam) is separated by around 42 m thick weak interburden parting from the No. 3 Seam (upper seam), which was extracted two decades earlier. During mechanised depillaring of Panel CM-1 of No.5 Seam, significant instability was observed beneath the overlying barrier pillars, including spalling of up to 1.5 m from both sides of the fenders, development of multiple roof cracks with apertures ranging from 3 mm to 30 mm, and early roof falls at several locations. Field monitoring indicated that induced vertical mining stress of up to 26.57 MPa was observed over a fender, posing a significant challenge for safe extraction. The effect of the instability is comprehensively studied combining numerical modelling, empirical analysis and strata monitoring. The findings of the analyses revealed that the overlying barrier pillars act as a stress concentrator and impose a significant amount of load towards the underlying working especially during splitting of a pillar. Numerical modelling predicted a maximum stress of 27.33 MPa, which closely agreed with the field-measured value, with an error of only 2.86%. Based on the findings, modifications in the manner of pillar extraction and an artificial support system were proposed to mitigate instability and ensure safe and efficient extraction of coal in the sub-sequent panels of the mine. This study highlights the influence of multiple seam interaction due to depillaring with caving even at moderate interburden thickness and emphasizes the need for site-specific design strategies in bord and pillar working under the influence of overlying barrier pillars.
